summary: Published the Mawia explicit-Mertens-sum node and reduced both reciprocal-prime nodes to it, collapsing two hand-written bounds into one citation.

new_node.statement: |sum_{p<=x} 1/p - log log x - B| <= 4/log^3 x  for x >= 2, where B = gamma + sum'_p (log(1-1/p) + 1/p)
new_node.source: R. Mawia (R. Vanlalngaia, Ramdinmawia), Explicit Mertens sums, 2017, zbMATH Zbl 1412.11125; statement as tabulated in the TME-EMT explicit-bounds wiki (Explicit bounds on primes, Art01, section 2): x >= 2 with constant 4, x >= 1000 with 2.3, x >= 24284 with 1. This node states the widest-range (constant 4) case.
new_node.numerical_sanity: A_1 = S - loglog x - B measured by sieve: 0.605 at x=2, 0.0807 at x=10, 3.897e-5 / 9.574e-6 / 4.030e-6 at x=10^6/10^7/10^8, all far inside 4/log^3 x (8.32, 0.328, 2.6e-3, 8.7e-4, 6.4e-4 respectively).

why_this_route.rejected: Deriving the reciprocal bound from TaoFivePrimes.schoenfeld_psi_error_large by Abel summation. The identity A_1(x) = (theta(x)-x)/(x log x) - integral_x^inf (theta(y)-y)(1+log y)/(y^2 log^2 y) dy turns a 1/log Chebyshev error into a 1/log error in A_1, crossing the allowance 1/(2 log^2 x) at x = 1.0668e8.
why_this_route.needed: A Chebyshev estimate with at least two powers of log in the denominator (|theta(y)-y| <= c y/log^2 y works for c <= 0.49), or directly an explicit Mertens sum bound with three logs - which is what Mawia's theorem provides.
why_this_route.consequence: No Abel-summation formalisation is needed at all: the numeric step 4/log^3 x < log(1 + 1/(2 log^2 x)) for x >= 10^8 is elementary and proved in both files.
